**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 satisfies the preferred position on all four elements:

- **§ 24.1** — Customer may assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only, assignee assumes obligations).
- **§ 24.2** — Vendor restricted asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent, with an absolute carve-out barring assignment to a direct Customer competitor.
- **§ 24.3** — Residual assignments subject to a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard; non-conforming attempts void.
- **§ 24.4** — Expressly no Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, plus a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes.

I also confirmed there is no back-door trigger elsewhere: § 9 termination rights run only to material breach and insolvency, and § 9.2 states that a lawful reorganization is not by itself grounds for termination. Supporting provisions reinforce the position — § 13 permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor on a Section 24 assignment, and § 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for a permitted successor. The "Affiliate" definition (§ 1.1) uses a standard >50% voting control test, which is workable for us.
